name: John Paul Jones
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Led Zeppelin with Jimmy Page in 1968 at age 22, after becoming one of London's most in-demand session musicians and arrangers from 1964 onward.
early_history_summary: Born to a musical family in Sidcup, Kent; his father was a pianist and arranger for big bands and his mother was also in the music business. He began piano at age six, joined his first band at 15, and landed his big break at 16 playing with Jet Harris and Tony Meehan of the Shadows. By 1964 he was doing extensive session work for Decca Records, playing on hundreds of recordings and arranging for major artists.
family_context_summary: Born into a musical family; father Joe Baldwin was a pianist and arranger for big bands including Ambrose and his Orchestra, and mother was also in the music business, with the family performing together as a vaudeville comedy act.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional pianist and arranger who taught Jones piano from age six, providing direct domain expertise and industry fluency in the British music scene.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musical family, session musician pipeline, London 1960s rock scene, father arranger
evidence_summary: John Paul Jones was born into a deeply musical family: his father was a professional big-band pianist and arranger who taught him piano from age six, and his mother also worked in music. He was playing in bands by 15 and became a top London session musician by 18, working with the Rolling Stones, Donovan, and Dusty Springfield. His deep arranging and multi-instrumental skills, honed through years of daily studio sessions, made him an ideal co-founder for Led Zeppelin at 22. The 1960s British rock explosion provided a powerful structural wave.
starting_point: Born to a musical family in Sidcup, Kent; father was a professional big-band pianist and arranger, mother also worked in the music business.
current_position: Retired from active touring but remains an influential musician; net worth estimated in the tens of millions; resides in the UK.

trajectory.event: Hired by Jet Harris and Tony Meehan of the Shadows, landing his first major professional gig.
Began extensive session work with Decca Records, becoming one of London's most in-demand session bassists and arrangers.
Co-founded Led Zeppelin with Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Bonham.
Led Zeppelin's debut album released, establishing the band as a major force in rock.
Led Zeppelin IV released, featuring 'Stairway to Heaven,' becoming one of the best-selling albums of all time.
Led Zeppelin disbanded following the death of drummer John Bonham.
Formed Them Crooked Vultures with Dave Grohl and Josh Homme, releasing a debut album.

name: Alexei Leonov
milestone_by_age_26: Selected to the first Soviet cosmonaut training group in 1960 at age 26, but his material milestone — the first human spacewalk — occurred in March 1965 at age 30. No material, independently verifiable achievement by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in a small Siberian village; his father was arrested in 1936 as an 'enemy of the people.' Leonov trained as a fighter pilot and made his first solo flight in 1955. He was selected to the first cosmonaut group in 1960, but his historic spacewalk came five years later.
family_context_summary: Born in Listvyanka, Siberia; father was an electrician and veteran who was arrested in 1936 as an 'enemy of the people' before rejoining the family years later.
evidence_summary: Leonov was selected to the first cosmonaut training group in 1960 at age 26, but his defining achievement — the first spacewalk — did not occur until 1965 at age 30. Selection to a training program, while significant, does not constitute a material milestone in the sense required by this rubric.

name: Katarina Taikon
milestone_by_age_26: Appeared in a minor documentary short film at age 16 in 1948, but her material achievements — founding the Roma Society, leading demonstrations, and publishing her influential book series — all occurred in the 1960s when she was over 30. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born into a Kalderash Romani family living in camps in Sweden; she did not learn to write until age 26. She was married off at 14 and ran away, finding work in a shop. She appeared in a documentary at 16 and acted in several Swedish films over the next decade, but her defining activism and writing came much later.
family_context_summary: Born to a Kalderash Romani family in a camp near Örebro, Sweden; father was a copper and silversmith who advocated for Romani education; mother died when Katarina was one year old.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a coppersmith and silversmith who advocated for Romani children's education from the 1930s, though the family lived in camps and faced severe discrimination.
evidence_summary: Taikon's early life was marked by extreme adversity as a Romani child in Sweden, denied schooling and married off at 14. Her minor film appearances in the late 1940s and 1950s were not material milestones. Her defining work — civil rights activism, founding the Roma Society, and her influential Katitzi book series — all came after age 30 in the 1960s-70s.

name: Juha Mieto
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver medal in the 30km at the 1974 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Falun at age 24, establishing himself among the world's elite cross-country skiers.
early_history_summary: Born in Kurikka, Finland; joined the local club Kurikan Ryhti. He competed at the 1972 Olympics at age 22, placing fourth in the 15km by just 0.06 seconds. He won the Holmenkollen 50km in 1973 and took World Championship silver in the 30km in 1974.
family_context_summary: Born in Kurikka, Finland; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his local club affiliation.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Finnish skiing culture, early competition, endurance specialization
evidence_summary: Mieto emerged from Finland's deep cross-country skiing tradition, competing internationally by his early 20s. His fourth-place finish at the 1972 Olympics at age 22 — losing bronze by 0.06 seconds — demonstrated elite-level performance. His World Championship silver in 1974 at age 24 confirmed his status. Family background and early training details are not well documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Kurikka, Finland; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing; served as a Finnish parliament member; resides in Finland.

trajectory.event: Competed at the Sapporo Olympics, finishing fourth in the 15km by just 0.06 seconds.
Won silver medal in the 30km at the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Falun.
Won Olympic gold in the 4x10km relay at the Innsbruck Winter Olympics.
Won two Olympic silver medals in the 15km and 50km at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics.
Won Olympic bronze in the 4x10km relay at the Sarajevo Winter Olympics in his final Olympic appearance.

name: Al Pacino
milestone_by_age_26: Pacino's first major professional role came in 1967 at age 27 (Charles Playhouse, Boston), his Obie Award was in 1968 at age 27, and his Tony Award in 1969 at age 29. No material milestone by age 26 (April 1966) found.
early_history_summary: Born in East Harlem to Italian-American parents who separated when he was two; raised by his mother and grandparents in poverty. He trained at HB Studio under Charlie Laughton and later at the Actors Studio under Lee Strasberg, but was often unemployed or homeless in his early 20s. His mother died in 1962 and his grandfather in 1963, which he called the lowest point of his life.
family_context_summary: Born to Italian-American parents in East Harlem; father left when Pacino was two; raised by his mother and maternal grandparents in poverty in the South Bronx. Mother died at 43 when Pacino was 22.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to acting or entertainment documented; parents were working-class Italian immigrants.
evidence_summary: Pacino trained seriously at HB Studio and the Actors Studio in his early 20s but had no professional breakthrough before age 26. His first major paycheck came in 1967 at age 27, his Obie Award in 1968 at 27, and his Tony Award in 1969 at 29. The Godfather stardom came at 32. Despite eventual legendary status, no material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Lars Hörmander
milestone_by_age_26: Completed his PhD thesis 'On the theory of general partial differential operators' at Lund University in 1955 at age 24, published in Acta Mathematica — a foundational work that eventually led to his 1962 Fields Medal.
early_history_summary: Born in Mjällby, Blekinge, Sweden; father was a school teacher. A teacher at his gymnasium who was also a docent at Lund University encouraged him to study university-level mathematics. He earned his master's degree at 19, completed his licentiate at 20, and finished his PhD at 24 with a groundbreaking thesis on PDE theory.
family_context_summary: Born in a small fishing village in southern Sweden; father was a school teacher. The youngest of five children. His talents became apparent very early — he skipped two years of elementary school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a school teacher, providing an educational environment, but no specific mathematical domain expertise in the family is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lund University pipeline, Marcel Riesz mentor, early prodigy, gymnasium acceleration
evidence_summary: Hörmander showed exceptional mathematical talent from childhood, skipping two years of elementary school. A gymnasium teacher who was also a Lund University docent taught him university-level mathematics while still in secondary school. He earned his master's at 19 and completed his groundbreaking PhD thesis at 24 under the influence of Marcel Riesz and Lars Gårding at Lund University. His thesis on PDE theory, published in Acta Mathematica in 1955, was foundational and directly led to his Fields Medal in 1962.
starting_point: Born in Mjällby, a small fishing village in Blekinge, Sweden; father was a school teacher; youngest of five children.
current_position: Died on November 25, 2012 at age 81 in Lund, Sweden; final role: professor emeritus at Lund University.

trajectory.event: Awarded master's degree from Lund University, having studied under Marcel Riesz.
Completed licentiate degree with a thesis on Helly's theorem applications.
Completed PhD thesis on general partial differential operators, published in Acta Mathematica.
Awarded the Fields Medal for his contributions to the theory of linear partial differential equations.
Appointed professor at Stanford University and then the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
Returned to Lund University as professor, where he remained until retirement.
Awarded the Wolf Prize in Mathematics.
Died on November 25, 2012 in Lund, Sweden.

name: Emilio Correa
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in welterweight boxing at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 19, defeating János Kajdi of Hungary 5-0 in the final — Cuba's first welterweight boxing gold.
early_history_summary: Born in Cuba; began boxing at age 14 in his local gym. By 18 he was selected for the Cuban national team and won gold at the 1971 Pan American Games in Cali, Colombia. At 19 he won Olympic gold at the 1972 Munich Olympics, knocking out defending champion Manfred Wolke en route to the final.
family_context_summary: Family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his Cuban origin and local gym training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban boxing system, national team selection, early specialization, Olympic pipeline
evidence_summary: Correa began boxing at 14 in his local Cuban gym and within four years was selected for the national team, winning Pan American Games gold at 18 and Olympic gold at 19. Cuba's state-sponsored amateur boxing pipeline provided elite training, facilities, and competition access from a young age. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. His rapid rise from local gym to Olympic champion in five years reflects both physical talent and the effectiveness of the Cuban boxing system.
starting_point: Born in Cuba; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on March 11, 2024 at age 70; final role: retired Cuban amateur boxer and boxing figure.

trajectory.event: Won gold medal in welterweight at the Pan American Games in Cali, Colombia.
Won Olympic gold medal in welterweight at the Munich Olympics, Cuba's first in that weight class.
Won gold medal at the World Championships in Havana and the Central American and Caribbean Games.
Competed at the Montreal Olympics but did not medal, exiting in the round of 16.

name: Ingemar Stenmark
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Cup race in December 1974 at Madonna di Campiglio at age 18, beginning a career that would yield 86 World Cup wins — the most by any male alpine skier in history.
early_history_summary: Born in Joesjö, Lapland, Sweden; moved to Tärnaby at age four. Began skiing at five and won his first national competition at eight. Made his World Cup debut in December 1973 at age 17, scoring points despite starting with bib 73. Won his first World Cup race in December 1974 at age 18 and won the overall World Cup title in 1976 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born in a small village in Lapland; family moved to Tärnaby when he was four. Family background beyond this is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources, but the family's relocation to Tärnaby, a skiing-focused community, provided early immersion in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tärnaby skiing community, early national competition, Swedish junior pipeline, technical mastery
evidence_summary: Stenmark grew up in Tärnaby, a small Swedish village near the Norwegian border that produced multiple elite skiers. He began skiing at five, won his first national competition at eight, and joined the Swedish junior national team at 13. His World Cup debut came at 17 with bib 73, and he won his first World Cup race at 18. The combination of geographic immersion in a skiing community, early specialization, and exceptional technical mastery made him the greatest technical skier in history.
starting_point: Born in Joesjö, Lapland, Sweden; family moved to Tärnaby when he was four, placing him in a community with a strong skiing tradition.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing since 1989; resides in Sweden; regarded as the greatest male technical alpine skier in history with 86 World Cup wins.

trajectory.event: Made World Cup debut in December, scoring points despite starting with bib number 73.
Won his first World Cup race in the slalom at Madonna di Campiglio, Italy on December 17.
Won the overall World Cup title, becoming the first Scandinavian to do so; also won Olympic bronze in giant slalom at Innsbruck.
Won gold in both slalom and giant slalom at the World Championships in Garmisch-Partenkirchen.
Won Olympic gold in both slalom and giant slalom at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics.
Won slalom gold at the World Championships in Schladming, becoming the first to win the same title in three consecutive world championships.
Retired from competitive skiing with 86 World Cup wins, the all-time record for any alpine skier.

name: Félix Savón
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold medal at the 1986 World Amateur Boxing Championships in Reno at age 19, the first of six consecutive World Championship titles in the heavyweight division.
early_history_summary: Born in San Vicente, Guantánamo Province, Cuba; made his ring debut in 1980 at age 13. Won his first important titles in 1985 including the Junior World Championships at age 18. Inspired by fellow Cuban Teófilo Stevenson, he won his first senior World Championship gold in 1986 at 19.
family_context_summary: Born in San Vicente, Guantánamo Province, Cuba; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his rural Cuban origin.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources, though inspiration from Teófilo Stevenson as a countryman is noted.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban boxing system, Stevenson inspiration, early ring debut, state-sponsored training
evidence_summary: Savón began boxing at 13 in Guantánamo and was inspired by his countryman Teófilo Stevenson. Cuba's state-sponsored amateur boxing system provided elite training, facilities, and competition from a young age. He won the Junior World Championships at 18 and his first senior World Championship gold at 19, beginning a streak of six consecutive world titles. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. His physical attributes — 6'5" with an 82-inch reach — combined with the Cuban pipeline to produce one of the greatest amateur boxers ever.
starting_point: Born in San Vicente, Guantánamo Province, Cuba; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from boxing in 2000; resides in Cuba; regarded as one of the greatest amateur boxers of all time with three Olympic golds and six World Championship titles.

trajectory.event: Won the Junior World Championships, his first major international title.
Won gold at the World Amateur Boxing Championships in Reno, his first of six consecutive world titles.
Won Olympic gold in heavyweight at the Barcelona Olympics.
Won Olympic gold in heavyweight at the Atlanta Olympics.
Won Olympic gold in heavyweight at the Sydney Olympics, his third consecutive Olympic title.

name: Srirasmi Suwadee
milestone_by_age_26: Entered service as a lady-in-waiting to Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn in 1993 at age 22, but her material milestone — marriage to the Crown Prince and royal title — came in 2001 at age 30. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born to a family of modest means in Samut Songkhram Province, Thailand. She attended Bangkok Business College and entered the service of Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn in 1993 at age 22 as a lady-in-waiting. She did not marry the Crown Prince until 2001.
family_context_summary: Born to a family of modest means in Samut Songkhram Province; third of four children born to Apiruj and Wanthanee Suwadee.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family had no prior royal or political connections documented.
evidence_summary: Srirasmi was born to a modest family and entered royal service at 22 as a lady-in-waiting, but her material milestone — marriage to the Crown Prince and acquisition of royal title — did not occur until 2001 at age 30. Her entry into royal service at 22 was an employment arrangement, not a material achievement. She later divorced in 2014 and was stripped of her royal titles.

name: Shotaro Ishinomori
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first professional manga 'Nikyuu Tenshi' (Second-Class Angel) in Manga Shōnen magazine in December 1954 at age 16, launching a career that would make him one of the most prolific and influential manga artists in history.
early_history_summary: Born Shotaro Onodera in Tome, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. He discovered manga through Osamu Tezuka's 'New Treasure Island' and began creating doujinshi around age 12. He contributed four-panel manga to Manga Shōnen magazine and published his first professional work at 16. In 1956 he moved to Tokyo and became Tezuka's assistant at Tokiwa-so, working on Astro Boy.
family_context_summary: Born to Kotarou and Kashiku Onodera in Ishinomori-Cho, Tome, Miyagi Prefecture; family background beyond this is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to manga or publishing identified.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tezuka mentorship, Manga Shōnen contest, Tokiwa-so community, early professional debut
evidence_summary: Ishinomori was a teenage prodigy who began creating manga around age 12, publishing doujinshi and contributing to magazines. His first professional work appeared in Manga Shōnen at 16, impressing Osamu Tezuka enough to earn a telegraph invitation to work as Tezuka's assistant. Moving to Tokyo at 18, he joined the Tokiwa-so apartment community of manga artists under Tezuka's mentorship, working on Astro Boy. This apprenticeship with the 'God of Manga' provided extraordinary early training and network access in the nascent manga industry.
starting_point: Born Shotaro Onodera to Kotarou and Kashiku Onodera in Ishinomori-Cho, Tome, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan; family background not documented beyond this.
current_position: Died on January 28, 1998 at age 60 in Bunkyō, Tokyo; final role: manga artist and founder of Ishimori Productions, having created over 770 titles and 500 volumes.

trajectory.event: Published his first professional manga 'Nikyuu Tenshi' in Manga Shōnen magazine.
Moved to Tokyo and became assistant to Osamu Tezuka at Tokiwa-so, working on Astro Boy.
Published 'Flying Phantom Ship,' later adapted into an animated feature film.
Created 'Cyborg 009,' the first superpowered hero team in Japanese manga.
Kamen Rider tokusatsu TV series launched, becoming a massive franchise.
Won the Shogakukan Manga Award for Hotel and Manga Nihon Keizai Nyumon.
Died on January 28; posthumously awarded the Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize.

name: Amparo Muñoz
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss Universe 1974 in Manila at age 20, becoming the first and only Spaniard to hold the title.
early_history_summary: Born in Vélez-Málaga, Spain to a blacksmith father and a housewife; the firstborn of six children. Her family's poverty led her godparents to help raise her from age seven. After high school she worked as an administrative assistant at a local newspaper, where the director encouraged her to enter a beauty contest. She won Miss Spain 1973 and then Miss Universe 1974.
family_context_summary: Born to a blacksmith father and housewife mother in Vélez-Málaga; firstborn of six children. Family poverty was severe enough that godparents helped raise her from age seven.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to entertainment, modeling, or beauty pageants documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, newspaper director encouragement, beauty pageant pipeline, Miss Spain to Miss Universe
evidence_summary: Muñoz grew up in poverty in Vélez-Málaga, raised partly by godparents. After working as an office assistant, her newspaper's director encouraged her to enter a local beauty contest, which led to winning Miss Spain 1973 and then Miss Universe 1974 at age 20. Her physical appearance was the primary asset, but the pageant system provided the pipeline. No family advantages in entertainment or modeling are documented. She resigned the Miss Universe crown after six months.
starting_point: Born to a blacksmith father and housewife mother in Vélez-Málaga, Spain; firstborn of six children; family poverty led godparents to help raise her from age seven.
current_position: Died on February 27, 2011 at age 56 in Málaga, Spain; final role: former actress and beauty queen who had retired from public life.

trajectory.event: Won the Miss Spain contest in Lanzarote, earning entry to the Miss Universe pageant.
Won Miss Universe 1974 in Manila, becoming the first and only Spaniard to hold the title; resigned after six months.
Began a film acting career, appearing in Spanish comedies and dramas.
Starred in Carlos Saura's acclaimed film 'Mama Turns 100,' cementing her acting career.
Died on February 27 in Málaga, Spain, due to cerebral aneurysm complications.
